title: Turborepo
description: Define task pipelines, cache outputs, and run only affected packages in a JavaScript monorepo.

data.text: Turborepo is a task runner for monorepos. It reads your workspace graph, runs tasks in dependency order and in parallel, and caches the outputs so unchanged work is never repeated — locally or in CI.

`^build` means "run the build of every dependency first". `outputs` tells Turbo what to cache — if you omit it, a cache hit restores nothing and the next task fails. `persistent: true` is for long-running dev servers, which must opt out of caching.

data.title: Run only what changed
data.code:
npx turbo run build --filter=@acme/ui...   # the package and its dependencies
npx turbo run test --filter=...[HEAD^1]     # packages changed since the last commit
npx turbo run build --dry-run=json          # inspect the task graph
npx turbo login && npx turbo link           # enable remote cache

data.caption: Turborepo resolves dependencies, then caches task outputs
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Changed files] --> B[Compute affected packages]
    B --> C{Dependency order}
    C --> D[Build dependencies]
    D --> E[Build package]
    E --> F{Cache hit?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Restore outputs from cache]
    F -->|No| H[Run task and store outputs]

data.title: Cache correctness depends on inputs
data.text: Turbo hashes source files, environment variables, and dependency outputs. If a task depends on an env var, declare it in `env` or `globalEnv`; otherwise a cache hit can replay results produced with different configuration.

terms.definition: The dependency rules that decide which tasks run and in what order.
A shared cache (Vercel or self-hosted) so CI and teammates reuse each other's outputs.
A selector such as --filter=@acme/ui... that limits a run to one package and its deps.
A long-running task (dev server) that is never cached and runs until stopped.

items.question: Turborepo or Nx?
items.answer: Both provide task graphs and caching. Turborepo is deliberately small and lets you keep your package manager and scripts; Nx adds generators, plugins, and stronger project boundaries. Choose Turborepo for a light touch, Nx for an opinionated platform.

items.question: Does Turborepo replace my package manager?
items.answer: No. It orchestrates scripts defined in each package.json and works with npm, Yarn, and pnpm workspaces.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Turbo runs workspace tasks in dependency order and in parallel.
Declare outputs so cache hits can restore build artifacts.
Use filters to run only affected packages in CI.
Declare env vars that affect output or caching becomes unsound.
data.takeaway: The interview point is not the config syntax — it is that caching only works when inputs and outputs are declared correctly.
